sentences.text: A fossil is the preserved remains, or the preserved trace, of a living thing from long ago.
A bone, a shell, a tooth, a footprint, or the print of a leaf can all be fossils.
Most plants and animals never become fossils. They are eaten, or they decay.
Hard parts are saved more often than soft skin, though prints of leaves do exist.
One common path starts when a shell or bone is buried quickly in mud or sand.
Burial can protect it from weather and from some animals that would scatter it.
Over a long time, minerals in the water can fill tiny spaces or replace the original material.
The shape remains, but much of what you see in a museum may now be stone.
A footprint can be a fossil even though no body is there. It is a trace of an action.
Scientists study fossils to learn what lived, what it ate, and what the place was like.
Not every fossil is a dinosaur. Dinosaurs are only one famous group.
Sea creatures, insects, plants, and very small living things appear in the fossil record too.
In a stack of rock that has not been badly folded, deeper layers are usually older than the layers above them.
A fossil in a lower layer is usually from an earlier time than a fossil higher in that same stack.
Fossils are rare records. Chipping them out of a park or a cliff for a souvenir can destroy the record for everyone.

questions.prompt: What is this passage mostly about?

choices.text: How to carve a souvenir from any cliff
Why every bone becomes a dinosaur
How mud stops all plants from decaying
What fossils are and what they can tell us

questions.explanation: The passage defines fossils, explains one way they form, and says scientists use them to learn about past life. That whole subject is the main idea.

questions.prompt: Which example is a trace fossil, with no body left behind?

choices.text: A footprint
A tooth
A shell
A bone

questions.explanation: The passage says a footprint can be a fossil even though no body is there, because it is a trace of an action. Bones, shells, and teeth are body parts.

questions.prompt: In this passage, decay means what?

choices.text: To turn into a footprint
To rot or break down
To be buried in a museum
To fold a layer of rock

questions.explanation: The passage says most living things never become fossils because they are eaten or they decay. Here decay means to rot or break down.

questions.prompt: Why does quick burial help a shell become a fossil?

choices.text: It makes every soft animal turn to stone overnight
It proves the shell is a dinosaur
It protects the shell so the shape has a chance to be preserved
It lifts the shell into a higher, younger layer

questions.explanation: The passage says burial can protect remains from weather and from animals that would scatter them. A reader can connect that protection to a better chance of preservation.

questions.prompt: In an undisturbed stack of rock, which fossil is usually older?

choices.text: The one in the top layer
The one found loose on a path
The one that is only a leaf
The one in the deeper layer

questions.explanation: The passage says deeper layers are usually older if the rocks have not been badly folded. A fossil lower in that stack is usually from an earlier time.
